sweep_summary: Only one keyword-title item exists for bata1294 in Glottolog/Crossref and it is a misattribution: Rozwadowski 1897 'Der litauische Akzent in der Universitas linguarum Litvaniae' (Indogermanische Forschungen 7: 233-270) is about Lithuanian accent, irrelevant to Batak Dairi, paywalled at De Gruyter, priority none; Crossref record saved. only web lookups was available). The best statement actually read in this sweep is the already-held Adelaar 1981 (NUSA 10) sec. 2.6 'Accent', p.5, whose page image was re-rendered and checked for diacritics: penult default, schwa-penult shifts accent to the ultima (bəlgàh, bəlèn), long final V (from suffixal contraction) and -su/vocatives take final accent, with an explicit vowel-quantity hierarchy V̄ > V > ə governing placement rather than syllable structure. It confirms and refines the catalog's van der Tuuk 1864 coding but does not supersede it, since Adelaar's Dairi data come from van der Tuuk and the Manik dictionary rather than his own fieldwork.

new_statements.quote: 2.6 Accent. The accent is on the penultima, unless it contains /ə/, in which case the accent is on the ultima, even if here the V is /ə/, e.g. bəlgàh, bəlèn. A V̄ in the ultima takes the accent, which is the case only in polymorphemic words, e.g. bagīn kinigurūn. [...] The suffix -/sù/, which expresses an excessive, demands the accent: /əntor/+/sù/ yields əntorsù. Forms of address (vocatives) also have the accent on the ultimate syllable. [...] NB. Except in lexemes with a CəCəC structure we see that the place of the accent within the Da lexeme is determined by vowel length with the following hierarchic arrangement: V̄, V, /ə/; it is not the syllable structure which determines the place of the accent but the relative quantity of the vowels

new_statements.reading: Penultimate default; a penult containing schwa passes the accent to the final syllable (even when the final vowel is also schwa, e.g. bəlgàh, bəlèn); a long final vowel (only in suffixed/polymorphemic words, from contraction: bagīn, kinigurūn) attracts the accent; the excessive suffix -su and vocatives are accented finally. Adelaar's explicit generalisation is a vowel-quantity hierarchy V̄ > V > ə that decides accent placement, not syllable structure (closed vs. open). This confirms the catalog's van der Tuuk 1864 coding (schwa repels stress to the following syllable) and refines it: the conditioning is vowel quantity/quality, not consonantal syllable weight, which is a direct input to the 'weight-hedged' question. Caveat: Adelaar's Dairi data are drawn from van der Tuuk's Grammar and the Dairi-Pakpak(-Dutch) dictionary manuscript (Tindi Radja Manik), not from his own fieldwork, so this is a modern linguist's synthesis rather than an independent first-hand observation.
